newsitem.title: USA: Ecolab sees '97 EPS growth near 17 pct.
newsitem.headline: Ecolab sees '97 EPS growth near 17 pct.

text.p: Ecolab Inc chief executive officer Allan Schuman said Friday the company expects earnings per share to grow about 17 percent in 1997, in line with analysts' estimates.
"We'll probably come close to a 17 percent increase (in earnings per share in 1997)," he said in a telephone interview.
First Call's mean estimate for Ecolab is for an increase to $2.05 from $1.75 EPS in 1996.

The cleaning products manufacturer notes that 35 percent of its total U.S. sales come from products and systems introduced or modified within the last five years. At the company's shareholder meeting here this morning Schuman highlighted three products being launched in 1997.
The Water Care Services division is introducing Crystal Mate, used in the treatment of water and air conditioning cooling towers.
The Professional Products division is launching Asepticare TB-plus, an antimicrobial cleaner used in health care offices.
The Food and Beverage division is introducing tsunami, a treatment designed to kill microrganisms during the cleaning of fruits and vegtables.
Schuman said he expected international operating margins to continue to widen in 1997.

"I think we'll make further improvements in 1997," Schuman said. "We're trying to get an additional one percent a year. Our goal is to get up to between 13 and 14 percent. As we get mass in these places and roll out more new products, I think we can get that."
Ecolab's international business had a 7.0 percent operating margin in 1996 and a 6.3 percent margin in 1995.
Schuman said the rate of increase in Ecolab's sales and service associates would accelerate in 1997.

"I think we might do an eight percent increase in 1997, in that area," Schuman said. "We've got to inch our way up the hill of success, and the only way you can do that is by putting more people in the street."
The number of Ecolab's sales and service associates increased six percent in 1996 to 5,605, while total employees also increased six percent to 9,573.
